text:
maria: Quick experiment notes: comparing full INT8 vs per-layer partial quant (exclude embed + lm_head) on 7B. Latencies look good on average but p99 spikes when using static calibration ranges.

maria: FP16 baseline: p95 ~38ms, p99 ~110ms. full INT8: p95 ~62ms, p99 ~190ms. partial (exclude embed/lm_head): p95 ~44ms, p99 ~120ms.

dan: Wow that p99 delta is large. Which kernel backend did you run? custom int8 kernels or cublas-int8? sequence lengths?

maria: Mostly our custom int8 matmul kernels on A100-80. Seq lens tested: 8/32/128/512. The p99s correlate with odd sequence lens and some KV cache ops.

lee: Likely pathological codepath: when cached KV pages use different quant scales we end up doing dequant/req quant on read/write which blows up tail. Are we serializing KV in-place or materializing?

maria: Currently materialize+requant on KV read. Profiling snippet:
```
[prof] iter=204 step_latency_ms=46.1 kernel=matmul_int8 layer=10 time=0.92ms
[prof] kv_read_ms=3.6 kv_write_ms=2.8 dequant_ms=1.4
[prof] iter=205 step_latency_ms=182.9 kernel=matmul_int8 layer=3 time=5.1ms <-- hotspot, extra reshapes + fallback
```

nisha: Did you try hybrid FP8/INT8? attention layers sometimes prefer FP8 to hold dynamic range, while FFN can be int8. Also calibration dataset composition matters (long vs short contexts).

maria: Tried FP8 for first 6 layers, INT8 for rest. Average latency improved a bit vs full INT8, but eval quality dropped on repetition/lengthy prompts. Also runtime fell back to a slower kernel when alignment constraints weren't met for certain seq lengths.

dan: That kernel fallback explains tail. We should add a trace field for "kernel_fallback_reason" and incremental counters for num_dequant_ops and kv_serialization_ops.

maria: Agreed. Filed issue #1428. Short term mitigation: per-layer symmetric minmax calibration and group layers to share scales so KV reads don't force recompute. Config I'm testing: 
```
quant_profile: 
  exclude_layers: ["embed", "lm_head"]
  layer_groups: [[0,5],[6,13]]
  calib_method: "minmax_symmetric"
  force_fp16_kv_when_kv_bytes_gt: 524288
  allow_kernel_fallback: false
```

lee: A couple runtime heuristics to try:
- If (dequant_ms + kv_read_ms) > threshold, prefer FP16 kernel for that layer.
- Force KV serializer to store FP16 slices if kv_bytes > X to avoid repeated quant/dequant churn.

nisha: I'm queueing a nightly perf matrix (seq=8/32/512, batch=1/4/16) with the new quant_profile across p3dn-24 and a100-80. infra-bot can you schedule?

infra-bot: Scheduled nightly-job: quant-profile-sweep-173950 (job_id=qi-2026-09-07-99). Will run on a100-80 and p3dn-24, matrix seq=[8,32,512] batch=[1,4,16]. Results to /perf/artifacts/qi-2026-09-07-99.json.

maria: One extra observation: calibration skew when using mostly long-context examples pushes some head activations into overflow range under INT8 causing quality regressions. Going to try stratified calibration (mix short/long and sampling by prompt type).

dan: If we can emit per-layer scale histograms to traces, we can automerge adjacent layers that have similar scale distributions and mark outliers for FP8/FP16. I'll sketch a sampler and an autogroup heuristic.

maria: OK moving forward w/ per-layer exclusion for embed/lm_head + conservative grouping and adding flags to avoid kernel-fallback and to force FP16 KV serialization. I'll send a PR for runtime flags and the trace changes. /cc @lee @nisha

lee: thx, will review the PR. keep an eye on p99 for seq=512 especially.

nisha: Also will add quality test run in nightly evals to catch repeat/length regressions before rollout.

maria: Great. Will post follow-up with perf artifacts and a short table of results once infra job finishes.
